findings.failure_mode: untrusted path or missing file aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed error that the caller can handle
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> (or a typed domain error) and propagate with ? instead of unwrap

findings.problem: File I/O fused into a function that returns domain data (Vec<Record>), violating Data/Calculations/Actions separation
findings.failure_mode: the shell (fs::read_to_string) is inlined with parsing and domain construction, making the pure logic untestable without real files and preventing reuse where the data source is already in memory
findings.fix: split into two functions: a shell function load_shards(path) -> Result<Vec<Record>, E> that handles I/O, and a pure function parse_shards(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> that only parses

findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV row causes a panic instead of a typed parse error, allowing hostile input to crash the program
findings.fix: return Result from the function and use .map_err(|e| ParseError::InvalidValue(e.to_string())) or a similar typed error on parse, with .ok_or(ParseError::MissingField) for the index

findings.problem: as u16 is a lossy conversion from u32; values above 65535 silently truncate
findings.failure_mode: a valid u32 value like 70000 silently becomes 4464, corrupting domain data without any error or warning
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ParseError::ValueOutOfBounds) to fail fast with a typed error on overflow

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] are unchecked indexing on a split result
findings.failure_mode: an empty line or a line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields causes an IndexOutOfBoundsException panic
findings.fix: use split_once(',') and ok_or(ParseError::InvalidLine), or use .get(0) and .get(1) with ok_or for bounds-safe access

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is a side effect in the parsing/calculation layer
findings.failure_mode: logging is fused into domain data construction, making the pure logic non-deterministic, untestable in isolation, and producing I/O side effects inside what should be a pure computation
findings.fix: move all println! calls to the shell layer; the pure parse function should return only data or errors with no I/O

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() allocates a Vec<String> for every line; should use split_once for two-field comma grammars
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation per line, plus the collected Vec is only accessed by index (parts[0], parts[1]), making the allocation completely wasteful and the code harder to bound
findings.fix: use let (name, value_str) = line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::InvalidLine)?; and parse value_str directly without intermediate Vec

findings.problem: Record exposes raw String and u16 primitives; no parse boundary, no newtypes, no smart constructors
findings.failure_mode: callers anywhere in the codebase can construct Record { name: "".into(), value: 0 } or any invalid state directly, making illegal states representable and bypassing all validation
findings.fix: use newtypes like NamedName(String) with a smart constructor, or derive Record via a parse function that validates; hide the struct's public fields behind a constructor: pub fn new(name: &str, value: u16) -> Result<Record, ParseError>

findings.problem: load_shards returns Vec<Record> instead of Result, discarding all fallible operations
findings.failure_mode: every internal fallible operation (fs read, parse, index, cast) must panic or silently truncate because the function signature cannot express failure; callers have no way to distinguish success from partial success
findings.fix: change signature to pub fn load_shards(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> where LoadError is a typed enum covering I/O, parse, and overflow variants
